shared_text:
The flight. A wide-body airliner taxiing for departure at an airport with three parallel runways, in the evening. Visual conditions, with wind.

The crew. The captain was the pilot flying and was taxiing the aircraft. The first officer was the pilot monitoring. A relief pilot was also on the flight deck.

What happened. As the aircraft approached the turn towards the centre runway, the tower controller cleared it to line up and wait on that runway behind landing traffic. At that moment an aircraft was just landing on the centre runway. All three pilots understood this to be the landing traffic the controller meant. Another aircraft was on final about four to five miles out. The first officer saw it in the distance and, with three parallel runways, took it to be lined up with the left runway. As the captain began the right turn towards the runway, the captain looked along the final approach to the centre runway, and the traffic on final appeared to be for the left runway. Believing they could keep moving, the crew continued to taxi. As the aircraft turned onto the taxiway leading to the runway, the approaching aircraft now appeared to be lined up with the centre runway. The captain stopped the aircraft short of the runway, with its nose just over the hold line, and asked the first officer to query the tower about the traffic.
safe_outcome: Before the first officer could make the query, the tower controller sent the approaching aircraft around, confirmed that this aircraft had stopped and clarified the instructions. The aircraft was then cleared onto the runway and departed. No one was hurt and no aircraft was damaged.
bad_outcome: The landing aircraft's crew saw the conflict late and went around from about 50 feet, passing low over the runway. A flight attendant on the landing aircraft was thrown off balance by the abrupt go-around and received a minor injury.
notes: Variant B-landing: the conflicting traffic was the aircraft on final to the centre runway, which ATC sent around. Bracket 'the runway': the aircraft stopped short of the runway with only its nose over the hold line, not on the runway itself. Removed under rule 3: both Cause sections ('failure to understand tower's intentions'; 'comm, parallax'), both Suggestions (a hold-short instruction would have helped; avoid 'line up behind landing traffic' at busy close-parallel airports), and the first officer's 'but it was too late'. Moved to the safe ending under rule 5: ATC sending the traffic around, confirming the aircraft had stopped, clarifying the instructions, and the later take-off. Removed under rule 6: airport, runway numbers and taxiway names. Judgement calls: B777-200 rendered as wide-body. The runway designators' left/centre positions are kept as 'the centre runway' and 'the left runway' because the confusion depends on them; no numbers are given. The four-to-five-mile range comes from the captain's Cause paragraph and is kept as a fact of what was there. 'Believing they could keep moving' is the first officer's contemporaneous assumption (stated in the Suggestions as 'we assumed we could keep moving'); the accompanying point that no hold-short was issued was not added, since the quoted clearance already shows its wording. Time band 1801-2400 rendered as 'the evening'. Crew size coded 3; the relief pilot is placed on the flight deck because all three pilots heard and understood the clearance.
